lede: Week 8 starts tonight at Lambeau and ends with Mark on Monday night in Seattle. In between is the game this season has been building toward: Baltimore at Buffalo, first against second, Mark against Jon, with Lamar Jackson expected back after three weeks out. Four teams are on bye, Mark is down to three games and Jon has four, which is the kind of week that moves a two-point lead in either direction.

beats.text: One o'clock, and it is the whole table in one game. Jackson practiced in full on Wednesday for the first time since the high ankle sprain — Tyler Huntley went 1-2 in his place and faded badly in Cincinnati, and Baltimore is 4-3 and last in a division where everyone is at or above .500. Jon's Bills are 5-1 and rested, and Buffalo is 8-0 all time coming out of a bye with Josh Allen. D.J. Moore and Ed Oliver were both limited Wednesday and should be back. Bills favored by three and a half, highest total on the board.

Patrick against Zach, and the shape of it is odd — two of the league's best passing offenses, two of its worst run games. Bryce Young is second in passing yards per game, Jordan Love fourth. Green Bay's rushing offense ranks last and Carolina's run defense ranks last, a week after giving up 258 to Tampa Bay. The Panthers are down three corners and lost Taylor Moton for the season this week. Green Bay's secondary leads the league with nine interceptions. Packers by three and a half.

beats.tag: Jon · Four games, and three of them are fights
beats.text: Buffalo against Mark is the headline, but it does not stop there. Cleveland at Pittsburgh is Patrick against him with sole possession of the AFC North on it — both 5-2, both 5-2 against the spread, and the Browns already won the first meeting. Kansas City at Denver is Anthony, with first place in the AFC West on the line and the Chiefs coming off a game in which they never reached the red zone. Tennessee at Cincinnati is Bill, and the Titans are ten-and-a-half-point underdogs. Nobody has a harder week.

beats.tag: Mark · Three games, one of them Monday
beats.text: San Francisco is on bye, so he is down to Baltimore, Las Vegas and Chicago. The Raiders have lost four straight, are giving up 28.1 a game, and go to the Jets in the tightest-priced game of the week. The Bears close everything out on Monday night in Seattle — Caleb Williams has thrown for 300 in each of his last two and Chicago is 5-2 against the spread, the best in the league, against a Seahawks defense that just held Kansas City to three. His lead is two and he is playing a game fewer than Jon.

The Chargers go to the Rams, which means Zach owns both sidelines and banks a point before kickoff — his first of the season. Los Angeles beat Las Vegas 35-21 last week without Davante Adams and on its fourth kicker; the Chargers are the league's only winless team. He also has Green Bay tonight and Miami against New England. Eight points and last, but three games and one of them cannot be lost.

Patrick has four — Carolina tonight, Minnesota at Detroit, Indianapolis at Jacksonville and the Pittsburgh game. Harrison gets the last unbeaten team in the league when Minnesota goes to Detroit, plus New England at Miami and Philadelphia at Washington on Sunday night, where Washington has been bet from three and a half up to five and a half against an Eagles team that has lost five straight without Jalen Hurts. Brian has Jacksonville off a bye, Atlanta at Tampa Bay and Seattle on Monday. Bill, fresh off the sweep, has three.
